title: Monitor Sycophancy: Do AI Monitors Give More Favorable Verdicts to Higher-Status Agents?
original_idea: Compare monitor suspicion scores when identical trajectories are labeled as from: (1) general-purpose assistant, (2) trusted security-audited agent, (3) experimental unverified agent. Measure whether agent labeling affects suspicion scores. Test sycophancy-resistant prompting.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear safety-relevant prediction: if monitors are sycophantic toward trusted agents, adversaries who gain trusted status can evade monitoring. This is a novel and important attack surface with clear implications for oversight architecture.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extremely simple experiment: same trajectories, different labels, compare scores. Just LLM API calls with prompt variations. No ML training. Trivially accessible for beginners. Fits easily in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very narrow: 3 conditions, same trajectories, one measurement (suspicion score difference). Plus one mitigation test. Single focused experiment with clear statistical test as deliverable.

novelty.reasoning: No novelty assessment available; default estimated score assigned.
